reviews.review: A meticulously detailed simulation of every day life in Australia.

EDF 5 is probably the best EDF game I've played to date and at the same time, I would prefer 4.1 or 2025...

The main changes to the classes were all great for the most part but some changes really ruined it for me.

Ranger: This guy is still largely tossed aside and under the bus and to make things worse he's shafted by certain weapons just feeling very weak now, like snipers being ok rather than powerful at times.
At least shot guns felt better, having inherent penetration.
His support kits are helpful but maybe he should have had 2? like a call-in and an armour kit? It just feels pointless when many vehicles are kind of pitiful and his armour kits are way more useful.

Wing Diver: I didn't play wing diver much on any title but I like the new core mechanic, the weapon variety, however the charge mechanics for some weapons is irritating and the damage falloff is downright horribly stupid by design and I'm surprised it was kept past initial release.

Fencer: What could you say about fencer? This class probably benefited the most from his changes and didn't take near any negatives. His dashing was made a part of the class, whilst removing the more cheesy dash cancel and he likely only suffers from the weakening of weapons that they confusingly did overall.

Air Raider: The second most benefited class I believe, many may think he got the best but he has one pivotal piece missing.
I play air raider the most in every title I got the chance to and vehicles were one of my favourites. Vehicles feel and are noticeably weaker and some may argue but a railgun should be powerful to compensate for low ammo, a titans' main gun should decimate whatever it hits directly. Most lock-on missiles which vehicles happen to use are poor as well due to lacklustre homing combined with long flight time before actually tracking the enemy.
This affected /affects my play heavily, I like to ride vehicles and in solo they're essential when raider is a supporting class.

Unfortunately the problem largely seems to be lacklustre balancing to weapons and tools whilst enemies grow more powerful and it's disappointing that with so many improvements that they would fall on their face. To a cynical person, it would feel like they planned on selling dlc with powerful weapons...

Gameplay wise, it's EDF. You fight hordes of enemies with immense weapons in the best way possible and on higher difficulties get punished for mistakes or poor planning.
I really enjoy the battle damage on enemies, the larger locales, the scale is even bigger and the missions with your allies are amazing fun.

It's difficult to put into words as EDF would seem to be a bad game but puts the focus where it's needed and with a ton of cheesy and campy dialogue and story, it's great fun overall.

I would almost recommend others to play 4.1 over this given the weapon and more atrocious vehicle balancing but this review is for a game that's been out for years...
4.1 may have had very clear "meta" weapons, but at least you had free reign to play any style still without being largely ineffective.
